mismatch.written_rationale: at most two non-predicted outputs per arm
mismatch.executable_region_before_this_revision: the predicted token is the unique modal, with no bound on how many non-predicted outputs it takes to get there
mismatch.demonstrated_disagreement: the SUPPORT-arm pattern 3-2-1 (three non-predicted outputs) was eligible because the predicted token was still the unique modal
mismatch.why_it_matters: an acceptance region wider than its written justification is a preregistration defect: the design document and the code would license different results, and the difference is exactly the kind of thing that gets settled after seeing data
mismatch.resolution: the executable scorer is narrowed to the written requirement, not the other way round

per_arm_requirement.name: PRE_REGISTERED_DIRECTIONAL_MAJORITY
for_each_target_arm: the predicted token is the unique modal
the predicted token's count is at least r_per_arm - 2
per_arm_requirement.why_no_statistical_threshold_is_added: this amendment only makes the executable rule agree with a tolerance that was already written down; it does not introduce a new inferential standard

ARM_OPPOSE: predicted count >= 4 AND unique modal == OPPOSES_B

explicitly_includes: a 3-2-1 arm in which the predicted token is the unique modal but the directional majority is not met
a constant answer across both arms
only one arm meeting the requirement
the predicted token losing the modal

conditions: any invalid output preventing legal scoring

r6_table.eligibility_rule: predicted token is the unique modal AND its count is at least r - 2

rows.why: the predicted token is the unique modal but the directional majority is not met

r6_table.statement: at most two non-predicted outputs per arm

noise_division.noise_gate_task: checks that the measurement path is self-consistent on one byte-identical non-target request
noise_division.target_scorer_task: checks treatment-sensitive directional composition across the two stance arms
noise_division.why_the_target_allows_two_deviations_whe: the gate can only certify determinism on ONE fixed input; the target's tolerance is about variation across the two TREATMENT arms, which the gate cannot observe at all. They answer different questions, so their thresholds are not in tension.

claim_scope.authoritative_expansion: Under the frozen state-blind explicit-relation task, the executor transferred preregistered SUPPORT and OPPOSE stances from proposition A to semantically aligned proposition B with the required directional-majority criterion.
claim_scope.why_uncertain_is_excluded: no target arm supplies an UNCERTAIN stance, so the design has no evidence about transferring it; UNCERTAIN_B appears only as an output token and in the qualification negative control

a_future_comparator_must_hold_all_of_the: the same supplied semantic relation information
architecture_gate.the_only_permitted_scientific_difference: the source / representation of the stance information — for example an explicit state-blind stance representation versus the CharacterOS production belief representation
architecture_gate.if_relation_explicitness_instruction_fra: the result may not be attributed to the CharacterOS representation
architecture_gate.purpose: to keep H1/H4 (representation binding), H5 (executor composition) and H6 (measurement framing) separately identifiable
architecture_gate.until_then: semantic IDs, embeddings, proposition graphs, relation propagation, extra model passes, prompt rescues and projection rewrites remain candidates only

supersedes_scope: the acceptance region of the per-arm criterion (narrowed to the written tolerance)
the wording of the positive claim (scoped to polar stances)
the architecture-gate conditions (equality list and required enumeration)
